content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn how to play tennis, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a high-quality graphite racket (1 hour)
Step 2. Register for a local amateur tournament (30 minutes)
Step 3. Watch professional match highlights for inspiration (2 hours)
Step 4. Practice overhead smashes (1 hour)
Step 5. Take a lesson on proper serving technique (1 hour)
Step 6. Research local tennis clubs (45 minutes)
Step 7. Practice cross-court forehands (2 hours)
Step 8. Buy a pressurized can of tennis balls (15 minutes)
Step 9. Ask friends for club recommendations (20 minutes)
Step 10. Pay the annual club membership fee (10 minutes)
Step 11. Find a hitting partner on a mobile app (30 minutes)
Step 12. Reserve an indoor court for practice (5 minutes)
Step 13. Read the club's safety guidelines (15 minutes)
Step 14. Purchase comfortable athletic shoes (1 hour)
Step 15. Apply a new overgrip to the racket handle (10 minutes)
Step 16. Break in the new tennis shoes (3 days)
Step 17. Buy a tennis bag to carry gear (30 minutes)
Step 18. Watch a tutorial on the scoring system (20 minutes)
Step 19. Pack your tennis bag with water and towels (10 minutes)
Step 20. Play a full three-set practice match (3 hours)
Step 21. Perform post-match muscle stretching (20 minutes)
Step 22. Get the racket strings tensioned at a pro shop (2 days)
Step 23. Review the rules of tie-breakers (15 minutes)
Step 24. Practice the ball toss for serves (45 minutes)
Step 25. Check the tournament schedule (5 minutes)
Step 26. Decide on a budget for tennis gear (1 hour)
Step 27. Sign up for a weekend intensive clinic (15 minutes)
Step 28. Visit a sports equipment warehouse (2 hours)
Step 29. Purchase a moisture-wicking headband (5 minutes)
Step 30. Watch "Tennis Basics" online videos (1 hour)
Step 31. Practice backhand groundstrokes (90 minutes)
Step 32. Buy a specialized tennis sun visor (10 minutes)
Step 33. Purchase a large water bottle (5 minutes)
Step 34. Buy a pack of athletic socks (10 minutes)
Step 35. Fill the water bottle with electrolytes (5 minutes)
Step 36. Buy a set of vibration dampeners (10 minutes)
Step 37. Download a tennis score-tracking app (5 minutes)
Step 38. Practice flat and slice serves (2 hours)
Step 39. Attach a vibration dampener to the strings (1 minute)
Step 40. Attend a mandatory pre-tournament briefing (1 hour)
